**Finding submitted: T4C — deviation (walk-away territory), preferred-level cure.**

- **What the document says:** Section 9 contains only cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Customer cause-like triggers (9.3), plus a force-majeure exit (27.3). There is no Section 9.4 and no convenience right for either party, while Section 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" against a three-year term (8.1).
- **Why it fails fallback:** no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is expressly walk-away under the rule.
- **Cure (2 surgical ops):** new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term; and a conforming edit to Section 2.1 that keeps the no-reduction restriction but makes the take-or-pay commitment subject to Section 9.4 (avoiding a contradictory retained mechanic).
- **Already met:** Section 10.2 already requires refund of prepaid recurring Fees covering the post-termination period, so no duplicate refund language was added. No early-termination fee exists, so none needed capping.
